recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It preserves the already-applied security guidance and corrects the broken cross-reference that could otherwise prevent implementers from seeing the stylesheet security warning.
issue_request: FHIR-7289 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core documents issue from the 2015May ballot asking that security risks identified in CDA stylesheet use be verified where the FHIR document guidance recommends using document-specified stylesheets.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in svn revision 6211, represented by git commit 816144fbce3040b9ed59cb9ec01f23298275bd8b, which added the security page stylesheet warning and a documents-page security-note link. The substantive security warning was present, but the added document link used security.html#stylesheet while the target anchor was named stylesheets.
additional_context: Current source still includes source/documents.html and source/security.html in the main specification hierarchy/navigation. The security page explains that FHIR document stylesheets are CSS rather than executable CDA XSLT, while still warning about external CSS content and identifying/session information leaks. Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant community evidence altering this conclusion.
reconciliation: Changed source/documents.html to link to security.html#stylesheets, matching the existing source/security.html anchor and making the FHIR-7289 security note reachable from the document stylesheet guidance.
source_changes: source/documents.html: corrected the document stylesheet security-note link from security.html#stylesheet to security.html#stylesheets.
